page: Microsoft Azure FX4mds_v2 is a high-frequency, memory-intensive compute instance hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. The server is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at a base clock speed of 4.2 GHz across 2 physical cores and 4 dedicated virtual CPUs with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, alongside AES cryptography extensions.

The hardware configuration pairs 84.0 GB of system memory, delivering an unusually high 21.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is locally provisioned via a 236 GB NVMe SSD, providing fast scratch and temporary data performance without external storage attachments. The instance includes no discrete graphics processing units and allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark measurements indicate exceptional single-core compute performance, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2262.0, placing it in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems. Single-threaded data handling tests also reflect strength, with gzip compression reaching 34.59 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression achieving 14.25 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput and large-block memory transfers fall into lower performance tiers due to the 4-vCPU ceiling and uncached large-block read-write bandwidth constraints of 35.98 GB/sec and 25.58 GB/sec, respectively.

Given its high core frequencies and high memory-per-core density, the FX4mds_v2 is architecturally aligned with licensing-constrained relational databases, electronic design automation (EDA), in-memory analytics, and single-thread-dominated calculation workloads that require significant memory footprints without paying for excess core counts.

Local scratch storage is supported by an integrated 236 GB NVMe SSD. The processor features AVX-512, AMX matrix acceleration, and a 260 MB L3 cache. In benchmark tests, the instance demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2262.0 and strong single-threaded compression speeds. However, multi-core throughput and uncached large-block memory bandwidth remain limited by the low core count. The server is well suited for memory-heavy workloads constrained by per-core software licensing, electronic design automation, batch financial modeling, and high-frequency relational database processing.
